results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds two records that provide this information.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains multiple types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are several types, including [KCab-c(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open [KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, VFB indicates that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core, surface, posterior, anterior-posterior, middle, dorsal, and claw-count classes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum and a large descending axon that enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge, where the two giant fiber neurons connect across the midline, and at the axonal lateral bend.

The giant fiber neuron is classified as a [primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047097 "Open primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, and P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. 

Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, and Kim et al., 2020. 

VFB holds records showing the giant fiber neuron connects with various neuron types, including [adult VNC neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00059289 "Open adult VNC neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [thoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001983 "Open thoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047096 "Open secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch OFF hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049540 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [mesothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001985 "Open mesothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), primary neuron, [Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049542 "Open Notch OFF hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [prothoracic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00001984 "Open prothoracic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049539 "Open Notch ON hemilineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB2-4 lineage neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048927 "Open NB2-4 lineage neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049541 "Open Notch ON hemilineage secondary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [input/output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053396 "Open input/output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain").
